transcript.text: Bosch built-in microwave BFL524MS0B randomly stops part way through cooking, time still on the display. Opening and closing the door lets it carry on. Maybe once every few days.

That behaviour points to the door interlock system as the most likely cause, where the microwave thinks the door has opened even though it is shut. It could be a sticky latch, some grease blocking the hooks, or one of the internal microswitches acting up occasionally. To help narrow this down safely, please unplug the unit first and check for any food debris or grease in the door slots that might stop the latch from engaging fully. Then plug it back in and try running a cup of water on full power to see if it still stops mid-cycle or runs smoothly now.

I've already cleaned some grease from around the door hooks and latch slots. It still happened once since, so that didn't fully cure it. No smell, sparks or tripping, and everything else heats normally. I can't remove the unit from the housing, it's screwed into the tall unit. What next?

Since cleaning didn't resolve it, we need to test if the door latch mechanism itself is engaging properly under load. Please plug the microwave back in and run a cup of water on full power for about one minute to see if it stops mid-cycle again or runs smoothly. This simple check helps confirm whether the issue is an intermittent mechanical binding or something else entirely.

I haven't run the water test yet, but I can say it heats fine when it works, and the stop happens more when I close the door gently. Door also looks very slightly lower on the handle side, though I can't be sure. Is this likely the door switch, and should I get a Bosch engineer in?

Unplug it first and never remove the outer casing. It could be the door interlock switch, but given your observation about the handle side sitting slightly lower and stopping more when you close it gently, mechanical alignment is also a very strong possibility. Since you cannot remove the unit to inspect the internal linkage or switches safely, this points toward needing professional help. I would recommend getting a Bosch engineer in to check the door hinge tension and the interlock mechanism properly.
